posts.body_html:
Took a long break from posting on the forum, but now that I broke my camera this morning, it might be a bit longer before more pics are posted again.

Anyways, here's S. leucophylla var. alba 'yellow flower, thick neck' Washington Co, AL. I think earlier in the year, it produced traps that didn't look like an alba whatsoever, but now it has some alba-ish looking ones. Of course, this thing can get solid white during the fall under optimal conditions, but for now, I'll settle for these beautiful summer traps! To recap, leucophyllas don't usually produce nice summer traps for many of us west coast outdoor growers, but the washington Co, AL population in general consistently puts on a nice show for us this time of year. I suspect most if not all leucophyllas from Washington Co, AL have alata mixed into their genes somewhere down the line. Even if it was a dozen generations ago, alata genes help explain why these plants in particular produce nice summer traps.

Photos taken 7/3/17:

posts.body_html:
updated photos of S. leucophylla var. alba 'yellow flower, thick neck' Washington Co, AL. As we have been discussing in other posts in this forum, the washington Co, AL population in general might be a good candidate for leuco lovers who live in more northern climates and have a shorter grow season. These leucos can produce some outstanding summer traps, and under the same exact conditions, many other populations of leucophylla either produce smaller, less colorful traps, or they're in pure phyllodia mode. I think as long as you keep these washington Co, AL plants happy, they won't go into phyllodia mode, they'll just keep shooting out traps until the fall flush.

Photos taken 8/10/17. Normally, you don't see traps that look like this until the fall, but many washington Co, AL clones like this alba 'yellow flower, thick neck' plant, shoot out stunning traps for us mid to late summer:


A new trap, but not as white. These typically get whiter as the trap ages, but that also depends on your environment:

posts.body_html:
While not yet at its "whitest potential" here's a stand-out alba clone where the white stretches 2" down the petiole, it's pretty amazing! Under the right conditions, it's solid white all the way down! Photos taken 8/11/17:






This is one individual out of thousands that will help change the "face" of leucophyllas in the future.
